content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines reading json request bodies as part of building apis with django. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Request content types; Parsing JSON safely; Validating request shapes; Invalid JSON handling; Size limits and malformed input. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Request content types
items.text: Request content types is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Parsing JSON safely
items.text: Parsing JSON safely is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Validating request shapes
items.text: Validating request shapes is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Invalid JSON handling
items.text: Invalid JSON handling crosses an application boundary. Define the data contract, timeouts/failure behavior, authorization and retry/idempotency rules; verify with synthetic input and avoid live secrets in practice.

items.title: Size limits and malformed input
items.text: Size limits and malformed input shapes the presentation layer. Separate layout from business logic, escape untrusted output, provide meaningful empty/error states, and check semantic structure and keyboard usability.
